A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChessArena study. Their main text, appendices, tables, figures and equations support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and additional material in v4.

before.justification: v2 reports original chess competitions, fine-grained evaluations, post-training results and cross-domain evaluations, including Tables 1–4 and 16.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds training ablations, board-reconstruction measurements, another trained model and mixed-domain training comparisons.

M1.justification: v4 introduces a rank-based continuous-reward objective and alternative reward combinations as experimental training variants in Appendix C.4. The final two-stage SFT plus GRPO procedure and its discrete rewards remain unchanged; this pipeline is additionally applied to Seed-Coder-8B.

E1.justification: v4 adds mathematics and coding training data from Eurus-2-RL-Data for mixed-domain training, plus an explicit board-reconstruction evaluation requiring FEN output from move history. Conversely, MHPP and FullStackBench evaluations in v2 Table 16 disappear from v4 Table 20. The original chess evaluation coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v4 substantially expands training comparisons with reward alternatives, SFT-stage controls and Math-RL controls with and without Chess-SFT. Seed-Coder-8B-Instruct and its chess-trained counterpart join several chess comparisons. Some existing comparator entries disappear, including three Doubao-1.5 models from basic understanding and DeepSeek-V3 from Blitz move selection.

E3.justification: New protocols include a 100-sample board-reconstruction evaluation, continuous-reward training on 10,000 chess samples, and approximately 10,000-sample math/code/chess mixtures with specified proportions and Chess-SFT controls. The original chess sample counts, decoding settings and main training hyperparameters are retained; the new Stockfish configuration passage supplies disclosure rather than establishing a setting change.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's checkpoint comparisons and existing analyses, v4 adds reward and SFT ablations, game-termination breakdowns, errors stratified by tactical complexity, direct board-reconstruction testing and mixed-domain transfer controls. It also adds two ZebraLogic cases exposing reasoning failures and token-limit truncation. Earlier move-history analyses and training curves are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use Glicko rating deviations and 95% rating intervals. v4 introduces no new repeated-run or seed reporting, task-level uncertainty estimates or significance tests. Additional rating tables follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 adds Seed-Coder, ablation, reconstruction and mixed-training results. Existing entries also change: baseline/Chess-RL AIME2025 scores change from 21.56/23.54 in v2 Table 16 to 18.61/19.30 in v4 Table 20; Doubao-Seed-1-6-Thinking's Standard-mode legal-move percentage changes from 40.6 to 97.6 in the gameplay statistics. These are reported revisions, without an explanation establishing corrections or reruns. Most retained main chess scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 Appendix C.4 adds a mathematical definition of the rank-normalized continuous reward. The MAR definition and Appendix B's Glicko equations, matching objective and derivation remain substantively unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central platform, LLM chess-deficiency and Qwen3 chess-improvement claims remain. v4 broadens the stated training contribution to improvements in coding, mathematics and logical reasoning, and claims coding benefits from mixing chess into RL. v2 already reported some cross-domain transfer, so this extends an existing contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations connecting reward density to training stability, distilled-response diversity to move legality, and tactical complexity to errors. It explains the resource constraint behind single-step RL and acknowledges negative transfer on some coding and mathematics benchmarks. New ZebraLogic cases discuss failed self-correction and truncation. The original outcome-supervision and legal-move-dependence limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies Stockfish-8-linux, depth 20, default node limits and MultiPV=1, and documents data sources and mixture sizes for added experiments. The abstract changes the repository location and explicitly claims code-and-data availability. Existing core hyperparameters, hardware and training-time disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Ferreira's search-depth study and the ERNIE 5.0 report, while removing the MHPP and FullStackBench references. It removes the discussion of Hwang et al.'s RL bottlenecks but retains that citation elsewhere. The updated GameArena citation identifies the same work, and the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v4 edits the abstract and contribution wording, moves Related Work ahead of the framework description, consolidates Appendices E and F, and separates Limitations from Discussion. It adds acknowledgements, ethics and LLM-use statements. Much of the existing technical prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the single-column presentation with a two-column format and extensively rearranges tables and captions. Detailed puzzle results move into a combined appendix table, gameplay statistics are split into separate displays, and new termination and checkmate-failure figures appear. Existing board illustrations and training curves are retained but relocated and rearranged.

improvement.justification: Targeted training controls, direct board-reconstruction measurements and expanded failure analyses provide useful evidence absent from v2; explicit engine settings also improve reproducibility. The gain is limited by unexplained score revisions, reduced external-benchmark coverage and unchanged uncertainty reporting. The continuous-reward comparison additionally documents only 10,000 training samples versus 56,000 for the main recipe, limiting conclusions about reward choice alone.
